items.title: George Masso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: I worked for Lester Lanin, I worked for Peter Duchin

ctx.x: Exactly. That’s who I worked for. I worked for Lester Lanin, I worked for Peter Duchin, I worked for the Meyer Davis office, and you know, first of all it paid very well and secondly the quality of musicianship in those groups is very high. And I’m a song player anyway. I grew up playing that kind of music with my dad, who had a band. And it’s very challenging when you get with the right people, playing harmony lines on a lot of those show tunes. There’s a formula that’s used. You know, the trombone player plays…
In the typical society orchestra, I would imagine that professionalism was really important also, that you had to learn to be on time, to look right.
